The city council voted 6-3 on Tuesday to convert two downtown parking structures into mixed-use housing, citing a vacancy rate above 40 percent since 2021, though opponents countered that the study behind the vote sampled only weekdays and that weekend events still fill both garages. The conversion is expected to add 310 apartments—a fifth of them below market rate—with construction starting next spring if financing closes.

One why for the compression, at the fork: I attributed the 40 percent figure to the council's stated reasoning rather than stating it flatly, so the opponents' weekday-sampling objection reads as a rebuttal to a claim rather than a competing fact.
